title: Arizona's 5th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Arizona's 5th Congressional District is an open-seat race following the decision of incumbent Republican Rep. Andy Biggs to run for governor rather than seek re-election. The district, which covers parts of the East Valley including Chandler, Gilbert, Queen Creek, and Apache Junction, is rated as Solid Republican by nonpartisan analysts. Three Democrats — Brian Hualde, Chris James, and Elizabeth Lee — are competing in the July 21 Democratic primary, while former Pinal County Sheriff Mark Lamb and small-business owner Daniel Keenan are vying for the Republican nomination. The outcome will determine who succeeds Biggs in representing this conservative-leaning district in the U.S. House.
polling_note: No specific public opinion polls with numeric results were found for this race as of mid-2026. The New York Times maintains a poll tracker for Arizona's 5th District but had not yet reported any polls meeting its inclusion criteria. Prediction markets and news reports suggest the race leans Republican.

candidates.name: Brian Hualde
candidates.summary: Brian Hualde is a fourth-generation Arizonan, combat veteran, and pediatric nurse practitioner running as a Democrat. He served as a combat medic in Operation Iraqi Freedom and currently works at Phoenix Children's Hospital. His campaign focuses on accessible healthcare, public education, and border enforcement reform with a humanitarian approach.

candidates.name: Chris James
candidates.summary: Chris James is a descendant of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians and serves as President and CEO of the National Center for American Indian Enterprise Development. He held senior roles at the U.S. Treasury and Small Business Administration under President Obama and was appointed to federal advisory bodies under Presidents Trump and Biden. His campaign emphasizes economic growth, education, infrastructure, and protecting democracy.

She has worked at leading fertility clinics and lobbied on Capitol Hill for IVF protections. Her campaign focuses on Medicare for All, affordable housing, protecting reproductive rights, and fully funding public schools.

candidates.name: Mark Lamb
candidates.summary: Mark Lamb served as Pinal County Sheriff from 2017 to 2024 and was the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Arizona in 2024, losing the primary to Kari Lake. He describes himself as a 'constitutional sheriff' and an America First conservative who prioritizes border security, combating fentanyl trafficking, and defending the Constitution. He has been endorsed by President Donald Trump.

forecast.rationale: No numeric public opinion polls exist for this race as of mid-2026, so confidence is medium rather than high. However, the strongest available signal is the district's underlying partisan baseline: nonpartisan analysts rate AZ-05 as Solid Republican, and it is an open seat previously held by a Republican incumbent. This overwhelming partisan advantage points to a strong Republican favorite in the general election regardless of which candidate emerges from either primary. Among Republican candidates, Mark Lamb has the strongest profile — former Pinal County Sheriff, the 2024 Republican U.S. Senate primary nominee, and endorsed by Donald Trump — making him the most likely nominee and general-election winner. The predicted margin of roughly 22 points is consistent with a safe Republican district. This forecast is informational and reflects data available as of June 20, 2026, before the July 21 primaries.
